# Script reference

Every console function, method, class and pref of an engine built from `DefaultPlugins`, read from the script engines it makes: the server's and the client's. The pages are written by the `torque-script-reference` tool (`just script-reference`) and checked in, so a change to the scripts' surface shows as a change to them; CI fails when they are stale.

| Page | What it lists | Entries |
|---|---|---|
| [Functions](functions.md) | console functions, by namespace | 317 |
| [Methods](methods.md) | methods called on an object, by class | 331 |
| [Classes](classes.md) | console classes and the fields they add | 119 classes, 957 fields |
| [Prefs](prefs.md) | `$Pref::` globals with their defaults and ranges | 25 |
| [RPCs](rpcs.md) | the RPC functions and the shape of an RPC's message fields, from a sample | 3 |
| [From Lua](lua.md) | the functions and methods as a Lua script calls them | 648 |

## Reading an entry

- Each entry says which script engine has it: the **server**'s, the **client**'s or both.
- The usage text is what the native prints when it is called with the wrong number of arguments, and what `obj.dump()` lists. An entry made with `#[torque::function]` or `#[torque::methods]` also shows the rest of its doc comment (see [Script functions from Rust](../../script-functions.md)).
- An argument count is the number of arguments a script passes, not counting the function's name or a method's object.
- A class lists only the fields it adds; it has its parent's too. A default is shown only for a class declared in Rust with `#[derive(EngineClass)]`, where it is the declaration's; the original classes set theirs in code the tables do not hold. A range is what a write is clamped to.
- Names compare without case in a script, so the pages sort them without case.

## Opt-in plugins

These plugins are not in `DefaultPlugins`. What each adds is listed with the plugin's id beside it, since a game that does not add the plugin does not have it.

- `torque.hierarchy`: the scene hierarchy (in the default plugins, on in engine mode): the SceneObject methods that hang an object on another at a local pose, read the tree and delete a subtree, a server API
- `torque.gizmos`: debug drawing: lines, boxes, spheres, arrows, crosses and labels in world space
- `torque.zoom`: the zoom: the field of view and how fast it changes
- `torque.hosting`: joining by address or room code: the lookup natives of a join screen
- `torque.rope`: ropes: the RopeData datablock, the console functions that hang, push, reel and take down ropes between points or objects, and a server's ropeNet functions that make ropes every client shows
- `torque.props`: props: the PropData datablock and the Prop class, rigid bodies a server simulates and every client sees, the prop functions that spawn, push, freeze and read them, and the placement checks a game's own spawn commands make; the Joint class and the joint functions (tethers, winches, welds, hinges, grapples) and their check
- `torque.props-prediction`: prop prediction on a client: the props its own Player holds, stands on or pushes drawn where they will be, and the client functions that show a push or a spawn at once (never sent to the server)
- `torque.tcp`: TCP and HTTP from script: the TCPObject class (connect, listen, send and the line callbacks) and the HTTPObject class (get and post, HTTPS too), with caps on sockets and bytes per tick
- `torque.gui-layout`: flex and grid layout: the GuiFlexCtrl and GuiGridCtrl containers, which lay their children out by CSS's flexbox and grid rules

`LivePerfPlugin` also adds a function and a pref, but its two names are the game's choice, so there is nothing fixed to list.
